Per-band peak prevalence and modelled power, fit with the aperiodic model that
the BIC comparison selected for each modality (iEEG atlas → **knee**, source
HD-EEG → **fixed**; see `bic_knee_vs_fixed_bootstrap_ci.qmd`). Each normalized
channel PSD is fit once with its selected mode; specparam peaks are assigned to
canonical bands by centre frequency, following
@castanheira2025QuantifyingRhythmicArrhythmic. For each (channel, band):

- **peak prevalence** — a region's prevalence in a band is the fraction of its
  channels with at least one fitted peak in that band (i.e. the per-band
  detection rate);
- **modelled power** — the amplitude (log-power height above the aperiodic
  component) of the *highest* peak in the band. The region-level amplitude
  heatmap is the median over channels *that have a peak*, so detection rate and
  amplitude are not confounded; the cross-modal correlation additionally uses
  the zero-filled amplitude with rank statistics.

Channels are pooled to the 38 bilateral regions of the shared atlas; the two
modalities use the same 38 regions, so they can be paired directly. Regions are
grouped into lobe blocks (Occipital, Parietal, Frontal, Temporal, then Insula)
in the atlas ordering, and the y-axis labels are coloured by lobe (Occipital
red, Parietal green, Frontal blue, Temporal/Insula black), matching the
clustering-result heatmaps.

```{python}
#| label: helpers
def load_psd_csv(path):
    """Split a saved normalized-PSD table into (psd_matrix, freqs, metadata).

    Frequency columns are numeric-named; everything else is metadata. The index
    is the channel name.
    """
    df = pd.read_csv(path, index_col=0)
    num_cols = [c for c in df.columns if str(c).replace(".", "", 1).isdigit()]
    freqs = np.array([float(c) for c in num_cols])
    psd = df[num_cols].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    meta = df[[c for c in df.columns if c not in num_cols]].copy()
    meta.index = df.index
    return psd, freqs, meta


def assign_band(cf, bands=EEG_BANDS):
    """Canonical band name for a peak centre frequency; None if outside all bands.

    Half-open [lo, hi) except the last band, which is closed [lo, hi].
    """
    for i, b in enumerate(bands):
        if (b.lo <= cf < b.hi) or (i == len(bands) - 1 and cf == b.hi):
            return b.name
    return None


def channel_fit_quality(fg, channel_names, dataset):
    """Per-channel goodness of fit: R² and MSE of the full log-power model.

    R² is specparam's own ``gof_rsquared``; MSE is the mean squared residual in
    log10-power space, reconstructing the model from the fitted aperiodic and
    peak parameters (same construction as the BIC build doc).
    """
    freqs = np.asarray(fg.data.freqs, dtype=float)
    rows = []
    for i, (channel, result) in enumerate(zip(channel_names, fg.results)):
        ap = fg.modes.aperiodic.func(freqs, *np.asarray(result.aperiodic_fit, dtype=float))
        peak_params = np.asarray(result.peak_fit, dtype=float).ravel()
        peak = fg.modes.periodic.func(freqs, *peak_params) if peak_params.size else 0.0
        residual = np.asarray(fg.data.power_spectra[i], dtype=float) - (ap + peak)
        rows.append(
            {
                "channel": channel,
                "dataset": dataset,
                "gof_rsquared": result.metrics.get("gof_rsquared", np.nan),
                "mse_log10": float(np.mean(residual**2)),
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def fit_and_extract_peaks(path, dataset, mode):
    """Fit the selected aperiodic mode and return a tidy peak table.

    One row per fitted peak: channel, dataset, Region name, Lobe, mni_y, CF, PW,
    BW, band. Also returns the per-channel metadata (the prevalence denominator)
    and a per-channel fit-quality table (R², MSE).
    """
    psd, freqs, meta = load_psd_csv(path)
    meta = meta.assign(
        dataset=dataset,
        region=meta["Region name"].astype(str).str.strip("'"),
        mni_y=pd.to_numeric(meta["mni_y"], errors="coerce"),
    )

    fg = SpectralGroupModel(**SPECPARAM_SETTINGS, aperiodic_mode=mode, verbose=False)
    fg.fit(freqs, psd, freq_range=list(FREQ_RANGE), n_jobs=1)

    peaks = fg.get_params("peak")  # (n_peaks, 4): [CF, PW, BW, ID]
    peaks = np.atleast_2d(peaks)
    peak_df = pd.DataFrame(peaks, columns=["CF", "PW", "BW", "ID"])
    peak_df["ID"] = peak_df["ID"].astype(int)
    peak_df["channel"] = meta.index.to_numpy()[peak_df["ID"].to_numpy()]
    peak_df["band"] = peak_df["CF"].map(assign_band)
    peak_df = peak_df.dropna(subset=["band"])

    keep = ["region", "Lobe", "mni_y", "dataset"]
    peak_df = peak_df.merge(meta[keep], left_on="channel", right_index=True, how="left")
    channels = meta[["region", "Lobe", "mni_y", "dataset"]].reset_index(names="channel")
    quality = channel_fit_quality(fg, meta.index.astype(str), dataset)
    return peak_df, channels, quality


def channel_band_table(peak_df, channels, bands=EEG_BANDS):
    """One row per (channel, band): has_peak and the band's modelled power.

    modelled_power is the highest peak's amplitude in the band; channels with no
    peak in the band get has_peak=False and modelled_power=NaN (the amplitude is
    undefined where nothing was detected).
    """
    band_names = [b.name for b in bands]
    best = (
        peak_df
        .sort_values("PW", ascending=False)
        .drop_duplicates(["channel", "band"])
        .set_index(["channel", "band"])["PW"]
    )
    grid = (
        channels
        .assign(key=1)
        .merge(pd.DataFrame({"band": band_names, "key": 1}), on="key")
        .drop(columns="key")
    )
    grid["modelled_power"] = grid.set_index(["channel", "band"]).index.map(best)
    grid["has_peak"] = grid["modelled_power"].notna()
    return grid


def region_prevalence_power(channel_band):
    """Collapse channels to regions: prevalence and median modelled power per band."""
    g = channel_band.groupby(["dataset", "region", "Lobe", "band"], observed=True)
    out = g.agg(
        n_channels=("channel", "nunique"),
        prevalence=("has_peak", "mean"),
        # amplitude where detected (separates amplitude from detection rate)
        median_power=("modelled_power", "median"),
        mni_y=("mni_y", "mean"),
    ).reset_index()
    return out


def clustering_region_order(region_info_csv=REGION_INFO_CSV, lobe_order=LOBE_ORDER):
    """Top→bottom region order matching the clustering-result heatmaps.

    Regions are grouped into lobe blocks in ``lobe_order`` (Insula, absent from
    that tuple, falls to the end); within a lobe they keep the atlas region
    numbering. This reproduces ``pesco.experimental.plotting`` row order.
    """
    info = pd.read_csv(region_info_csv)
    info["region"] = info["Region name"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
    info["lobe"] = info["Lobe"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
    rank = {lo: i for i, lo in enumerate(lobe_order)}
    info["__lobe_rank"] = info["lobe"].map(lambda l: rank.get(l, len(lobe_order)))
    # stable sort keeps the atlas region order (encounter order) within each lobe
    return info.sort_values("__lobe_rank", kind="stable")["region"].tolist()


def region_lobe_map(region_info_csv=REGION_INFO_CSV):
    """Map each display region name to its lobe (for colouring y-axis labels)."""
    info = pd.read_csv(region_info_csv)
    region = info["Region name"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
    lobe = info["Lobe"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
    return dict(zip(region, lobe))


def save_lobe_colored(plot, paths, dpi=150):
    """Draw a heatmap, colour its y-axis region labels by lobe, save, return the figure.

    plotnine themes one colour across all tick labels, so the per-lobe colouring
    of the clustering heatmaps is applied on the drawn matplotlib axes instead.
    """
    fig = plot.draw(show=False)
    lobe_of = region_lobe_map()
    for ax in fig.axes:
        for label in ax.get_yticklabels():
            lobe = lobe_of.get(label.get_text())
            if lobe:
                label.set_color(LOBE_TEXT_COLORS.get(lobe, "black"))
    for path in paths:
        fig.savefig(path, dpi=dpi, bbox_inches="tight")
    return fig


def ordered_region_band(region_power):
    """Add ordered categoricals: band labels (δ→γ) and clustering-style regions.

    Returns the dataframe plus the y-axis category order (reversed lobe order, so
    the first lobe block — Occipital — sits at the top of the tile plot).
    """
    d = region_power.copy()
    # top→bottom = clustering order; plotnine draws the first category at the
    # bottom, so reverse to put Occipital at the top.
    y_order = list(reversed(clustering_region_order()))
    d["region"] = pd.Categorical(d["region"], categories=y_order, ordered=True)
    d["band_label"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["band"].map(BAND_LABELS), categories=BAND_LABEL_ORDER, ordered=True
    )
    d["dataset"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["dataset"], categories=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"], ordered=True
    )
    return d, y_order
```

```{python}
#| label: compute
peak_tables, channel_tables, quality_tables = [], [], []
for dataset, path in INPUT_CSV.items():
    pk, ch, q = fit_and_extract_peaks(path, dataset, SELECTED_MODE[dataset])
    peak_tables.append(pk)
    channel_tables.append(channel_band_table(pk, ch))
    quality_tables.append(q)

all_peaks = pd.concat(peak_tables, ignore_index=True)
channel_band = pd.concat(channel_tables, ignore_index=True)
channel_quality = pd.concat(quality_tables, ignore_index=True)
region_power = region_prevalence_power(channel_band)
region_power_ord, region_order = ordered_region_band(region_power)

# Persist the region-level table next to the model-selection outputs.
region_power.to_csv(
    specparam_dir / "specparam_peak_prevalence_modelled_power_by_region.csv",
    index=False,
)
all_peaks.to_csv(
    specparam_dir / "specparam_selected_model_peaks_by_channel.csv", index=False
)
```

```{python}
#| label: pairing
def pair_region_band(region_power, value, x="iEEG atlas", y="source HD-EEG"):
    """Wide table region×band with the value from each modality, + Spearman per band."""
    wide = region_power.pivot_table(
        index=["region", "band"], columns="dataset", values=value, observed=True
    ).reset_index()
    wide = wide.rename(columns={x: "x_value", y: "y_value"}).dropna(
        subset=["x_value", "y_value"]
    )
    wide["band_label"] = pd.Categorical(
        wide["band"].map(BAND_LABELS), categories=BAND_LABEL_ORDER, ordered=True
    )
    rows = []
    for name in BAND_ORDER:
        sub = wide[wide["band"] == name]
        if len(sub) >= 3:
            rho, p = stats.spearmanr(sub["x_value"], sub["y_value"])
        else:
            rho, p = np.nan, np.nan
        rows.append({"band": name, "spearman_rho": rho, "p_value": p, "n": len(sub)})
    return wide, pd.DataFrame(rows)


prevalence_pairs, prevalence_rho = pair_region_band(region_power, "prevalence")
```

```{python}
        ggplot(d, aes("band_label", "region", fill="prevalence"))
```

```{python}
def plot_prevalence_difference(prevalence_pairs, region_order):
    d = prevalence_pairs.copy()
    d["diff"] = d["y_value"] - d["x_value"]  # HD − iEEG
    d["region"] = pd.Categorical(d["region"], categories=region_order, ordered=True)
    lim = float(np.nanmax(np.abs(d["diff"])))
    return (
        ggplot(d, aes("band_label", "region", fill="diff"))
        + geom_tile(color="white", size=0.3)
        + scale_fill_gradient2(
            low="#B2182B", mid="white", high="#2166AC",
            midpoint=0, limits=(-lim, lim), name="HD − iEEG",
        )
        + labs(
            x="band", y="",
            title="Prevalence difference (source HD-EEG − iEEG atlas)",
        )
        + theme_bw()
        + theme(
            figure_size=(5.5, 9),
            axis_text_y=element_text(size=6),
            plot_title=element_text(size=11),
        )
    )


prevalence_diff_fig = save_lobe_colored(
    plot_prevalence_difference(prevalence_pairs, region_order),
    [
        fig_dir / f"peak_prevalence_difference_heatmap.{ext}"
        for ext in ("svg", "pdf", "png")
    ],
)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-prevalence-scatter
#| output: true
def plot_agreement_scatter(pairs, rho, value_name, title):
    strip = {
        BAND_LABELS[r["band"]]: f"{BAND_LABELS[r['band']]}\nρ={r['spearman_rho']:.2f}"
        for _, r in rho.iterrows()
    }
    d = pairs.copy()
    d["panel"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["band_label"].astype(str).map(strip),
        categories=[strip[lbl] for lbl in BAND_LABEL_ORDER],
        ordered=True,
    )
    color = {strip[BAND_LABELS[n]]: BAND_COLORS[n] for n in BAND_ORDER}
    return (
        ggplot(d, aes("x_value", "y_value"))
        + geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="#999999")
        + geom_point(aes(fill="panel"), size=2.2, alpha=0.8, stroke=0, show_legend=False)
        + scale_fill_manual(values=color, guide=None)
        + facet_wrap("panel", nrow=1)
        + labs(
            x=f"iEEG atlas\n{value_name}", y=f"source HD-EEG\n{value_name}",
            title=title,
        )
        + theme_classic()
        + theme(
            figure_size=(15, 3.3),
            panel_spacing=0.04,
            strip_background=element_blank(),
        )
    )


prevalence_scatter = plot_agreement_scatter(
    prevalence_pairs, prevalence_rho, "peak prevalence",
    "Cross-modal prevalence agreement (one point per region)",
)
for ext in ("svg", "pdf", "png"):
    prevalence_scatter.save(
        fig_dir / f"peak_prevalence_agreement_scatter.{ext}",
        width=15, height=3.3, dpi=150, verbose=False,
    )
```

## Peak centre frequency (band-edge check)

```{python}
#| label: fig-centre-frequency
#| output: true
def plot_centre_frequency(all_peaks):
    edges = band_edges()  # band lower edges + final upper edge
    d = all_peaks.assign(
        dataset=pd.Categorical(
            all_peaks["dataset"],
            categories=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"], ordered=True,
        )
    )
    return (
        ggplot(d, aes("CF", fill="dataset"))
        + geom_vline(xintercept=edges, linetype="dashed", color="#999999", size=0.4)
        + geom_density(alpha=0.45, color="none")
        + scale_x_continuous(breaks=[1, 4, 8, 13, 30, 50, 80])
        + labs(
            x="peak centre frequency (Hz)", y="density", fill="",
            title="Fitted peak centre frequencies vs canonical band edges",
        )
        + theme_bw()
        + theme(figure_size=(8, 3.5), plot_title=element_text(size=11))
    )


cf_fig = plot_centre_frequency(all_peaks)
for ext in ("svg", "pdf", "png"):
    cf_fig.save(
        fig_dir / f"peak_centre_frequency_distribution.{ext}",
        width=8, height=3.5, dpi=150, verbose=False,
    )
cf_fig
```

```{python}
def plot_peak_size_frequency(all_peaks, bins=40):

        + labs(
```

## Peak size vs centre frequency, per lobe

Same binned density, faceted by lobe (rows) and modality (columns). Each bin's
count is divided by the number of channels in that lobe and modality, so the
colour is **peaks per channel** and lobes of different size are comparable.

```{python}
#| label: fig-size-frequency-lobe
#| output: true
LOBE_FACET_ORDER = list(LOBE_ORDER) + ["Insula"]


def plot_peak_size_frequency_by_lobe(all_peaks, channel_band, bins=30):
    # Channels per (modality, lobe) is the normalisation denominator; taken from
    # the full channel list so channels with no peak still count.
    n_channels = (
        channel_band.assign(
            Lobe=channel_band["Lobe"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
        )
        .groupby(["dataset", "Lobe"], observed=True)["channel"]
        .nunique()
        .rename("n_channels")
        .reset_index()
    )
    d = all_peaks.assign(
        Lobe=all_peaks["Lobe"].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'")
    ).merge(n_channels, on=["dataset", "Lobe"], how="left")
    d["weight"] = 1.0 / d["n_channels"]
    d["Lobe"] = pd.Categorical(d["Lobe"], categories=LOBE_FACET_ORDER, ordered=True)
    d["dataset"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["dataset"], categories=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"], ordered=True
    )
    return (
        ggplot(d, aes("CF", "PW"))
        + geom_bin2d(aes(weight="weight"), bins=bins)
        + geom_vline(xintercept=band_edges(), linetype="dashed", color="#999999", size=0.25)
        + scale_fill_cmap(cmap_name="plasma", name="peaks per\nchannel")
        + facet_grid("Lobe ~ dataset")
        + scale_x_continuous(breaks=[1, 4, 8, 13, 30, 50, 80])
        + labs(
            x="peak centre frequency (Hz)",
            y="peak size (log-power height above aperiodic)",
            title="Peak size vs centre frequency per lobe (count per channel)",
        )
        + theme_bw()
        + theme(figure_size=(9, 12), plot_title=element_text(size=11))
    )


size_freq_lobe_fig = plot_peak_size_frequency_by_lobe(all_peaks, channel_band)
for ext in ("svg", "pdf", "png"):
    size_freq_lobe_fig.save(
        fig_dir / f"peak_size_vs_frequency_by_lobe.{ext}",
        width=9, height=12, dpi=150, verbose=False,
    )
size_freq_lobe_fig
```

## Dominant peak frequency per region

For each region and modality, the dominant frequency is the centre frequency of
the single highest-amplitude (largest PW) peak among that region's channels. The
dumbbell connects the iEEG and source HD-EEG dominant frequency for each region;
regions follow the same lobe order and label colouring as the heatmaps.

```{python}
#| label: fig-dominant-frequency-dumbbell
#| output: true
def region_dominant_frequency(all_peaks):
    """Centre frequency of the highest-PW peak per (modality, region)."""
    idx = all_peaks.groupby(["dataset", "region"], observed=True)["PW"].idxmax()
    return all_peaks.loc[idx, ["dataset", "region", "Lobe", "CF", "PW"]].reset_index(
        drop=True
    )


def plot_dominant_frequency_dumbbell(all_peaks):
    dom = region_dominant_frequency(all_peaks)
    y_order = list(reversed(clustering_region_order()))
    dom["region"] = pd.Categorical(dom["region"], categories=y_order, ordered=True)
    dom["dataset"] = pd.Categorical(
        dom["dataset"], categories=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"], ordered=True
    )
    # Wide form for the connecting segment (regions present in both modalities).
    wide = (
        dom.pivot_table(index="region", columns="dataset", values="CF", observed=True)
        .dropna(subset=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"])
        .reset_index()
    )
    wide["region"] = pd.Categorical(wide["region"], categories=y_order, ordered=True)
    return (
        ggplot()
        + geom_vline(xintercept=band_edges(), linetype="dashed", color="#cccccc", size=0.3)
        + geom_segment(
            wide,
            aes(x="iEEG atlas", xend="source HD-EEG", y="region", yend="region"),
            color="#bdbdbd",
            size=1.5,
        )
        + geom_point(dom, aes("CF", "region", color="dataset"), size=3, stroke=0)
        + scale_color_manual(values=DATASET_COLORS, name="")
        + scale_x_continuous(breaks=[1, 4, 8, 13, 30, 50, 80])
        + labs(
            x="dominant peak frequency (Hz)",
            y="",
            title="Dominant peak frequency per region (highest-amplitude peak)",
        )
        + theme_bw()
        + theme(
            figure_size=(8, 9),
            axis_text_y=element_text(size=6),
            plot_title=element_text(size=11),
            legend_position="top",
        )
    )


dumbbell_fig = save_lobe_colored(
    plot_dominant_frequency_dumbbell(all_peaks),
    [
        fig_dir / f"dominant_frequency_dumbbell.{ext}"
        for ext in ("svg", "pdf", "png")
    ],
)
dumbbell_fig
```

## Per-region peak-frequency distribution (ridgeline)

A joy-plot / ridgeline view built with `ridgenine` (`stat_binline` +
`geom_ridgeline`): one histogram ridge per region of the peak centre
frequencies, normalised so every region peaks at the same height (`ndensity`,
i.e. shape not count). `scale` sets how far neighbouring ridges overlap. Ridges
follow the heatmap lobe order, are filled by lobe, and the two modalities are
shown side by side.

```{python}
#| label: fig-region-frequency-ridges
#| output: true
def plot_region_frequency_ridges(
    all_peaks,
    binwidth=1.0,
    scale=1.2,
    alpha=0.6,
    title="Per-region peak-frequency distribution (histogram ridgeline)",
):
    region_order = clustering_region_order()  # top → bottom
    lobe_of = region_lobe_map()
    d = all_peaks.assign(lobe=all_peaks["region"].map(lobe_of))
    # Discrete y: plotnine draws the first category at the bottom, so reverse the
    # clustering order to put Occipital on top.
    d["region"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["region"], categories=list(reversed(region_order)), ordered=True
    )
    d["dataset"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["dataset"], categories=["iEEG atlas", "source HD-EEG"], ordered=True
    )
    d["lobe"] = pd.Categorical(
        d["lobe"], categories=list(LOBE_ORDER) + ["Insula"], ordered=True
    )
    return (
        ggplot(d, aes(x="CF", y="region", fill="lobe"))
        + geom_vline(xintercept=band_edges(), linetype="dashed", color="#dddddd", size=0.25)
        + geom_ridgeline(
            stat=stat_binline(binwidth=binwidth),
            scale=scale, color="white", size=0.2, alpha=alpha,
        )
        + facet_wrap("dataset", nrow=1)
        + scale_fill_manual(values=LOBE_COLORS, name="lobe")
        + scale_x_continuous(breaks=[1, 4, 8, 13, 30, 50, 80])
        + labs(x="peak centre frequency (Hz)", y="", title=title)
        + theme_ridges()
        + theme(
            figure_size=(10, 12),
            axis_text_y=element_text(size=6),
            plot_title=element_text(size=11),
        )
    )


ridge_fig = save_lobe_colored(
    plot_region_frequency_ridges(all_peaks),
    [fig_dir / f"region_frequency_ridges.{ext}" for ext in ("svg", "pdf", "png")],
)
ridge_fig
```

## Per-region peak-frequency distribution — high-quality fits only

The same ridgeline restricted to peaks from channels whose specparam fit passes
a goodness-of-fit screen: **R² > 0.9 and MSE < 0.1** (log10-power). R² > 0.9 is
the de-facto specparam/FOOOF threshold; specparam reports error as MAE rather
than MSE, so the MSE < 0.1 cut is the squared-residual analogue (stricter on
large local misfits). Channels failing either criterion drop out, so sparse or
poorly-modelled regions thin or disappear.

```{python}
#| label: fig-region-frequency-ridges-hq
#| output: true
R2_MIN, MSE_MAX = 0.9, 0.1

good_channels = channel_quality.loc[
    (channel_quality["gof_rsquared"] > R2_MIN)
    & (channel_quality["mse_log10"] < MSE_MAX),
    ["dataset", "channel"],
]
all_peaks_hq = all_peaks.merge(good_channels, on=["dataset", "channel"], how="inner")

ridge_hq_fig = save_lobe_colored(
    plot_region_frequency_ridges(
        all_peaks_hq,
        title=(
            "Per-region peak-frequency distribution "
            f"(R² > {R2_MIN}, MSE < {MSE_MAX})"
        ),
    ),
    [
        fig_dir / f"region_frequency_ridges_high_quality.{ext}"
        for ext in ("svg", "pdf", "png")
    ],
)
ridge_hq_fig
```

```{python}
#| label: hq-retention
#| output: true
n_total = channel_quality.groupby("dataset")["channel"].size()
n_pass = good_channels.groupby("dataset")["channel"].size()
pd.DataFrame(
    {"n_channels": n_total, "n_pass": n_pass, "fraction_pass": (n_pass / n_total).round(3)}
).reset_index()
```

## Sensitivity: alternative specparam settings

Refit from the (verified-clean) normalized PSD with a looser, EEG-tuned peak
configuration, leaving all results above unchanged. Only the specparam settings
differ; the selected aperiodic mode per modality is the same (iEEG knee, HD-EEG
fixed).

```{python}
#| label: alt-settings-refit
ALT_FREQ_RANGE = (1.0, 80.0)
ALT_SPECPARAM_SETTINGS = dict(
    peak_width_limits=[1, 12],
    max_n_peaks=8,
    min_peak_height=0.15,
    peak_threshold=2.0,
)


def refit_peaks(settings, freq_range):
    """Reload each normalized PSD, refit the selected mode, return peaks + quality."""
    peak_frames, quality_frames = [], []
    for dataset, path in INPUT_CSV.items():
        psd, freqs, meta = load_psd_csv(path)
        fg = SpectralGroupModel(
            **settings, aperiodic_mode=SELECTED_MODE[dataset], verbose=False
        )
        fg.fit(freqs, psd, freq_range=list(freq_range), n_jobs=1)

        pk = pd.DataFrame(
            np.atleast_2d(fg.get_params("peak")), columns=["CF", "PW", "BW", "ID"]
        )
        pk["ID"] = pk["ID"].astype(int)
        ids = pk["ID"].to_numpy()
        pk["channel"] = meta.index.astype(str).to_numpy()[ids]
        pk["dataset"] = dataset
        pk["region"] = meta["Region name"].astype(str).str.strip("'").to_numpy()[ids]
        pk["Lobe"] = meta["Lobe"].astype(str).to_numpy()[ids]
        pk["band"] = pk["CF"].map(assign_band)
        peak_frames.append(pk.dropna(subset=["band"]))
        quality_frames.append(channel_fit_quality(fg, meta.index.astype(str), dataset))
    return (
        pd.concat(peak_frames, ignore_index=True),
        pd.concat(quality_frames, ignore_index=True),
    )


all_peaks_alt, channel_quality_alt = refit_peaks(
    ALT_SPECPARAM_SETTINGS, ALT_FREQ_RANGE
)
```

```{python}
#| label: alt-settings-quality
#| output: true
def quality_summary(quality, label):
    g = quality.groupby("dataset")
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "settings": label,
            "median_r2": g["gof_rsquared"].median().round(3),
            "median_mse": g["mse_log10"].median().round(4),
            "pass_R2>0.9_MSE<0.1": (
                g.apply(
                    lambda d: ((d["gof_rsquared"] > 0.9) & (d["mse_log10"] < 0.1)).mean(),
                    include_groups=False,
                ).round(3)
            ),
        }
    ).reset_index()


pd.concat(
    [
        quality_summary(channel_quality, "default"),
        quality_summary(channel_quality_alt, "alt (wider peaks, lower thresh)"),
    ],
    ignore_index=True,
)
```

```{python}
    ),
```

## How `peak_threshold` and `min_peak_height` change detected peaks

Isolating the two detection thresholds (peak width fixed at `[1, 8]`): the
default `peak_threshold=3.0, min_peak_height=0.10` vs the looser
`peak_threshold=2.0, min_peak_height=0.15`. Example HD-EEG spectra are chosen
where the looser thresholds add the most peaks; each panel overlays the
normalized spectrum, both full model fits, and the detected peak centres
(markers on each model curve) so it is visible *where* in the spectrum the extra
peaks appear.

```{python}
#| label: fig-threshold-illustration
#| output: true
from plotnine import geom_line, scale_x_log10

SETTINGS_STRICT = dict(
    peak_width_limits=[1, 8], max_n_peaks=8, min_peak_height=0.10, peak_threshold=3.0
)
SETTINGS_LOOSE = dict(
    peak_width_limits=[1, 8], max_n_peaks=8, min_peak_height=0.15, peak_threshold=2.0
)
# Wider peaks + fewer peaks: lets one broad Gaussian cover a hump instead of
# tiling it with several narrow ones.
SETTINGS_WIDE = dict(
    peak_width_limits=[1, 10], max_n_peaks=8, min_peak_height=0.15, peak_threshold=2.0
)
LAB_STRICT = "thr 3.0 / min_h 0.10 / w[1,8]"
LAB_LOOSE = "thr 2.0 / min_h 0.15 / w[1,8]"
LAB_WIDE = "thr 2.5 / min_h 0.15 / w[2,12] / max 6"
ILLUS_DATASET = "source HD-EEG"
N_EXAMPLES = 6


def fit_group(path, mode, settings):
    psd, freqs, meta = load_psd_csv(path)
    fg = SpectralGroupModel(**settings, aperiodic_mode=mode, verbose=False)
    fg.fit(freqs, psd, freq_range=list(FREQ_RANGE), n_jobs=1)
    return fg, meta


def model_curve(fg, i):
    """Full log-power model (aperiodic + peaks) for spectrum i."""
    freqs = np.asarray(fg.data.freqs, dtype=float)
    r = fg.results[i]
    ap = fg.modes.aperiodic.func(freqs, *np.asarray(r.aperiodic_fit, dtype=float))
    pp = np.asarray(r.peak_fit, dtype=float).ravel()
    peak = fg.modes.periodic.func(freqs, *pp) if pp.size else np.zeros_like(freqs)
    return ap + peak


fg_strict, meta_ill = fit_group(
    INPUT_CSV[ILLUS_DATASET], SELECTED_MODE[ILLUS_DATASET], SETTINGS_STRICT
)
fg_loose, _ = fit_group(
    INPUT_CSV[ILLUS_DATASET], SELECTED_MODE[ILLUS_DATASET], SETTINGS_LOOSE
)
fg_wide, _ = fit_group(
    INPUT_CSV[ILLUS_DATASET], SELECTED_MODE[ILLUS_DATASET], SETTINGS_WIDE
)
freqs_ill = np.asarray(fg_strict.data.freqs, dtype=float)
n_strict = np.array([len(r.peak_fit) for r in fg_strict.results])
n_loose = np.array([len(r.peak_fit) for r in fg_loose.results])
n_wide = np.array([len(r.peak_fit) for r in fg_wide.results])
examples = np.argsort(-(n_loose - n_strict))[:N_EXAMPLES]
channels = meta_ill.index.astype(str).to_numpy()

fits = [(fg_strict, LAB_STRICT), (fg_loose, LAB_LOOSE), (fg_wide, LAB_WIDE)]
line_rows, point_rows = [], []
for i in examples:
    panel = f"{channels[i]}  (n {n_strict[i]}/{n_loose[i]}/{n_wide[i]})"
    data = np.asarray(fg_strict.data.power_spectra[i], dtype=float)
    curves = {lab: model_curve(fg_, i) for fg_, lab in fits}
    for f, d in zip(freqs_ill, data):
        line_rows.append((panel, f, d, "spectrum"))
    for lab, curve in curves.items():
        for f, v in zip(freqs_ill, curve):
            line_rows.append((panel, f, v, lab))
    for fg_, lab in fits:
        pk = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(fg_.results[i].peak_fit, dtype=float))
        for cf in (pk[:, 0] if pk.size else []):
            point_rows.append((panel, lab, float(cf), float(np.interp(cf, freqs_ill, curves[lab]))))

KIND_ORDER = ["spectrum", LAB_STRICT, LAB_LOOSE, LAB_WIDE]
KIND_COLORS = {
    "spectrum": "#999999",
    LAB_STRICT: "#2C7FB8",
    LAB_LOOSE: "#E8546B",
    LAB_WIDE: "#1B9E77",
}
line_df = pd.DataFrame(line_rows, columns=["panel", "freq", "power", "kind"])
line_df["kind"] = pd.Categorical(line_df["kind"], categories=KIND_ORDER, ordered=True)
point_df = pd.DataFrame(point_rows, columns=["panel", "kind", "CF", "power"])
point_df["kind"] = pd.Categorical(point_df["kind"], categories=KIND_ORDER, ordered=True)

threshold_fig = (
    ggplot(line_df, aes("freq", "power", color="kind"))
    + geom_vline(xintercept=band_edges(), linetype="dashed", color="#e6e6e6", size=0.25)
    + geom_line(size=0.6)
    + geom_point(point_df, aes("CF", "power", color="kind"), size=2.4)
    + facet_wrap("panel", scales="free_y")
    + scale_color_manual(values=KIND_COLORS, name="")
    + scale_x_log10(breaks=[1, 4, 8, 13, 30, 80])
    + labs(
        x="frequency (Hz)",
        y="log10 power (normalized)",
        title=(
            "Peak detection: strict vs loose thresholds vs wider peaks "
            "(panel n = strict/loose/wide)"
        ),
    )
    + theme_bw()
    + theme(figure_size=(12, 7), legend_position="top", plot_title=element_text(size=11))
)
for ext in ("svg", "pdf", "png"):
    threshold_fig.save(
        fig_dir / f"peak_threshold_minheight_examples.{ext}",
        width=12, height=7, dpi=150, verbose=False,
    )
threshold_fig
```
